item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mixed, leaning negative. In 2024 AMLO did allow some scrutiny to proceed in specific cases, especially Ayotzinapa and a few anti-corruption actions, but the stronger pattern was hostility toward independent oversight: attacks on journalists, pressure on transparency institutions, and retaliatory scrutiny of critics.

- [Presidente AMLO entregará informe a madres y padres Ayotzinapa con anexos que sustentan cada respuesta](https://www.gob.mx/segob/prensa/presidente-amlo-entregara-informe-a-madres-y-padres-ayotzinapa-con-anexos-que-sustentan-cada-respuesta-370094) - Secretaría de Gobernación, 2024-07-03. The government said it had carried out searches at 251 sites in 2024 and would deliver a report with supporting annexes to the families; this is evidence of continued investigation and case handling rather than simply closing the file. `7B.6`

- [Versión estenográfica conferencia de prensa del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador del 24 de junio de 2024](https://www.gob.mx/amlo/articulos/version-estenografica-conferencia-de-prensa-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador-del-24-de-junio-de-2024) - Presidencia de México, 2024-06-24. AMLO said he had no proof the Army was responsible for Ayotzinapa, that if proof appeared “se actúa,” and that he had not exonerated anyone. This is weak but real evidence that he did not fully shut down inquiry. `7B.6`

- [Gobierno federal presenta caso de evasión fiscal de Totalplay; debe más de mil 500 millones de pesos al SAT](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/gobierno-federal-presenta-caso-de-evasion-fiscal-de-totalplay-debe-mas-de-mil-500-millones-de-pesos-al-sat/) - Presidencia de México, 2024-03-15. AMLO publicly backed the SAT/SCJN action against a politically connected firm and framed it as a concrete tax-evasion case, which is evidence of at least some willingness to publicize and pursue scrutiny of powerful business actors rather than automatically protect them. `7B.6`, `7B.4`

- [Mexico](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico) - Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, 2024-06-17. This source cuts both ways: it says Xóchitl Gálvez obtained a court-ordered right of reply to false claims AMLO made, showing an independent legal remedy still worked, but it also says AMLO’s final year featured regular attacks on journalists and the NYT phone-number episode. `7B.6`, `7B.2`

- [Mexico: Proposed Constitutional Changes Threaten Rights](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-08-30. HRW said the reform package would abolish the transparency watchdog and weaken judicial independence, which would make independent investigation of conduct, conflicts, and concealed decisions much harder. `7B.6`, `7B.2`, `7B.4`

- [Escala pugna de AMLO contra Loret y Latinus por investigación de la UIF](https://www.am.com.mx/nacional/2024/6/25/escala-pugna-de-amlo-contra-loret-latinus-por-investigacion-de-la-uif-709854.html) - Periódico AM, 2024-06-25. Latinus accused AMLO of using the state apparatus and the UIF to target it after reporting on corruption and funding irregularities involving family, collaborators, and friends; AMLO denied ordering a probe of Loret, but the episode still reads as retaliatory pressure on independent scrutiny. `7B.6`, `7B.2`, `7B.4`

- [Mexico](https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-net/2024) - Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House said the government used insecurity to justify expanded surveillance with little accountability and that a covert SEDENA cyberspace unit monitored critics; that is strong negative evidence on tolerance of outside investigation and exposure of hidden decisions. `7B.6`, `7B.2`

**Search Gap**  
I did not find strong 2024 evidence that AMLO voluntarily opened his own assets or campaign-finance records to independent audit. The record is mostly indirect: pressures on transparency institutions, attacks on journalists, and selective responses to investigations of allies and critics.
